verdict.rationale: Jan's source is public on GitHub (janhq/jan) and calls itself an "Open-source ChatGPT replacement". The docs repeat the open-source claim, and the README has build-from-source instructions, so users can read and build the code. Missing for 10: the specific license is never named or quoted (no OSI license identifier or LICENSE file cited), and there is no independent corroboration of the licensing terms.
